pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT ALERT · High KV cache eviction rate · cluster=rtx-prod · severity=page

maya (oncall): acked. getting graphs now. latency p95 for text-gen is up ~450ms from baseline, and eviction rate is through the roof on rtx-1/3. lots of cache churn.

aj: are these evictions due to TTL storms or memory pressure? any big deploys?

maya (oncall): no deploys in the last hour per opsbot. memory usage per node shows spikes right before evictions. TTL distribution looks normal. suspect a hotspot model/route.

opsbot: deploy-log · no prod deploys in last 90m. autoscaler: scaled up gpus at 1798001170.

devon: pinging logs for eviction reasons. tailing worker logs now:
```
WARN KVCache Evictor: evicted 1200 entries (node rtx-1) reason=LRU memory_exceeded
INFO KVCache: current_size_bytes=3.9GB threshold=4GB
```

liam: hmm if the threshold is being hit we may be evicting hot prefixes. that's bad for latency. can we bump cache limit temporarily?

maya (oncall): trying a hotfix: increasing cache max to 6GB on rtx-1/3 via ansible playbook (runbook step 2). will report back.

aj: while that's rolling, can we add a fallback to read-through to S3 for requests that miss excessively? maybe enable small short-circuit to a lower-cost path to avoid tail spikes.

maya (oncall): enabling read-through fallback for model group alpha-prod now. command: `kubectl patch cm kv-config -p '{"data":{"max_cache_bytes":"6442450944"}}'`

opsbot: playbook started: apply-cache-config to rtx-1/rtx-3 · job=jb-3147 · status=running

sarah-eng: adding my +1 to dashboards. right now we only have a single "cache hit rate" panel aggregated by cluster. need per-node and per-route breakdowns and eviction rate panel.

devon: cache config patch applied to rtx-1, rtx-3. seeing immediate drop in evictions but hit rate still low for a few models (alpha*: ~62%). latency p95 falling slowly.

liam: looks like one model traffic spike is causing a hot prefix — could be a repeated prompt pattern. can we sample requests hitting that model? add logging for prefix hash.

maya (oncall): sampling enabled for alpha-prod/model-v3 for 1k requests.

pagerduty-bot: NOTE: customer-impact assessment requested. impacted customers: a small subset of PLG tier apps using alpha-models experienced elevated tail latency and a couple of timed-out generation requests. severity: degraded.

aj: good that impact is limited. we need to tune alerts so we don't page for transient eviction bursts but still page for sustained degradation. current alert: `kv_cache_eviction_rate > 50` (per cluster) for 5m -> page. that's too chatty.

sarah-eng: proposed change: split alert into two tiers: Warning (non-pager) if eviction_rate > 30% for 5m OR hit_rate < 75% for 5m; Page if eviction_rate > 40% for 10m AND hit_rate < 65% for 10m OR p95_latency_increase > 200ms for 5m. Also add "eviction_surge" mute rule for autoscaler events.

maya (oncall): I agree. created a temporary pager mute rule for autoscaler-caused spikes while we tune.

devon: created a Grafana dashboard draft: panels = [node_eviction_rate, route_eviction_rate, cache_hit_rate (per-route), ttl_distribution, memory_usage_by_node, recent_evicted_prefixes]. Query snippets: `sum by(node) (rate(kv_evictions_total[1m]))` and `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(kv_request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))`.

aj: can we also add an alert for eviction-to-hit correlation? e.g., if eviction_rate_up 2x and hit_rate_down > 20% within 5m, fire non-pager and annotate runbook.

liam: acknowledge. I'll add an alert rule that creates an "eviction_correlation" annotation with `eviction_rate / hit_rate` metric and severity label.

maya (oncall): current state: evictions down ~70% since cache bump, p95 latency down ~180ms but not yet to baseline. sampled requests show repeated prefix hash collisions for one client. reached out to support to throttle abusive client.

pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT update · status=mitigated · mitigations=cache_bump,read_through_fallback,sampling · time_to_mitigate=12m

sarah-eng: next steps (post-incident):
- formalize per-route cache dashboards and add them to the "prod-kv-cache" dashboard folder
- add eviction alerts with two-stage paging logic (warning -> page)
- implement eviction-aware fallback behavior in runtime (avoid evicting hot prefixes)
- set SLO: maintain cache hit rate >= 85% for 95% of routes during business hours
- create runbook section: "Cache eviction surge" with immediate actions and playbook commands

aj: also recommend a follow-up to evaluate quantization/size tradeoffs per-model so we don't OOM caches for a few hot models. assign to infra-research.

devon: opened GH issue rfk/infra#842: "KV cache: per-route dashboards + eviction alerts + runbook" and assigned to sarah-eng + liam.

maya (oncall): handing off to aj for long-term tuning, I'll remain available for 15m for any rollback. thanks team. :thumbsup:

aj: taking over handoff. will coordinate with observability for alert rollouts and schedule a 30m tuning sync tomorrow.

opsbot: runbook checkpoint saved · link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-eviction-surge

maya (oncall): closing thread on on-call side. please update the incident postmortem when you have timeline + metrics.

liam: logged action items in the incident board.

sarah-eng: copying recommended alert rule (prometheus style) here for follow-up:
```
alert: KVCacheHighEviction
expr: (
  sum by(cluster) (rate(kv_evictions_total[5m])) > 0.4 and
  avg_over_time(kv_cache_hit_rate[10m]) < 0.65
)
for: 10m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "Sustained high KV cache evictions and low hit rate"
```

maya (oncall): thanks everyone. postmortem assigned to devon. we'll review root cause: cache sizing + hotspot traffic pattern + alert tuning.

pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED · root_cause=hotspot_prefix + cache_size_thresholds + alerting_thresholds · responders=[maya (oncall), aj, devon, liam, sarah-eng]
